channel.title: The Daily Free Press - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Daily Free Press (dailyfreepress.com)

item.title: BU students overcome with whimsy on rare snow day
item.description: If you grew up somewhere cold, chances are you’ve wished for a snow day before.

item.title: Blood-spangled banner | Con-Current Events
item.description: We Americans now have to live with new norms: The possibility of being kidnapped or murdered by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers, being ignored by Trump’s Federal Emergency Management Agency when a catastrophic climate event occurs or the possibility of being gunned down in our classrooms, with Federal Bureau of Investigation Director Kash Patel too incompetent to prevent or catch the perpetrators.

item.title: The threat to free speech isn’t suppression — it’s retaliation | Editorial
item.description: The incident was not an anomaly, but rather a public manifestation of a growing reality on college campuses: Coordinated political harassment campaigns aimed to intimidate, silence and punish free speech through both personal and reputational harm.

item.title: Are protests effective? BU professor, student activists respond
item.description: As protests against the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement ramp up in Minneapolis and across the country, BU professors and students with backgrounds in activism emphasized the impact protests can have.

item.title: BU President Melissa Gilliam emphasizes interdisciplinary research initiatives in presidential address
item.description: Boston University President Melissa Gilliam delivered her first annual presidential address Wednesday afternoon at the Tsai Performance Center, announcing efforts to further BU’s reputation as a leading research institution through continued support of interdisciplinary initiatives.

item.title: SPH study puts a ‘magnifying glass’ on 46.6 million Americans living within a mile of fossil fuel infrastructure
item.description: Most Americans in cities aren’t passing high-polluting power plants or oil rigs on their commute to work or walk to class. However, other potentially dangerous components of the fossil fuel production process that aren’t visible to average passersby such as transport, storage and refinement could be closer to home than previously thought.

item.title: BU’s hot start extinguished in 58-50 loss to Navy
item.description: The Boston University men’s basketball team was edged out by the league-leading U.S. Naval Academy on Wednesday night, the final score settling at 58-50.

item.title: Let the Games Begin: The next step for U.S. figure skating
item.description: A new era of winter sports begins next week. Feb. 6 marks the start of the 25th Olympic Winter Games, hosted by Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo. For the U.S. figure skating team, it’s a chance to showcase the program’s resurgence since the last Olympics.

item.title: At her live performance in Cambridge, Izzy Pingrey knows many faces
item.description: The walls of Isabella Pingrey’s dorm room are adorned with photos of her friends. Outside the door and down the hallway of her Student Village suite, her roommates can be heard cracking jokes and laughing.

item.title: Trump and BU: A year in review
item.description: The Daily Free Press constructed a timeline of events at Boston University which were affected or caused by the Trump administration in the first year of Trump’s second term.
